Title: Fabric_Normal Map
Content: Normal Map Normal Map - Apply Normal Map images to express uneven texture more realistically. Adjust Intensity -Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. - Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material Texture to see its child menus. Then, expand the Normal Map option as well. - Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map using the Intensity option. - When the Normal Map Intensity values is adjusted from 0, CLO will automatically create a Normal Map and express the texture more realistically. Apply Normal Map Images Via Property Editor - The custom made Normal Maps can be applied to the fabric items as well. - Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. - Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material Texture to see its child Menus. - Click the icon next to the Normal Map. The Open File browser will appear. - Locate the desired Normal Map image and click Open. - Adjust the intensity values to express the texture more realistically. Via Drag &amp Drop - From the PCs Browser window, drag and drop a Normal Map image to the Browser button next to the Normal Map option. Apply with Desired Map Type - From the PCs Browser window, drag and drop an image file to an object where the image should be applied to. - The Texture Map Type window appears. Choose the desired Map type and select OK. Save Auto-generated Normal Map - Normal Map generated when adjusting Intensity can now be saved. - Adjust the Intensity under the Normal Map option. - Navigate to Main Menu File Save as Surface Textures and locate the saving path. - Select Original size or Crop size when saving. - The Normal Map can be saved when exporting as OBJ,FBX,LXO. Note: Normal Map and Roughness Map are retained even if Texture is deleted.(ver.4.2)

Title: Texture Generator (ver 7.1)
Content: List of Contents Open Texture Select Area of Texture Set Options Save Texture Image Apply Texture Objective Seamlessly generate texture maps with scanned or captured images, and check the results in real-time within the 3D window. Location Object Browser Fabric Texture Generator Operation Open Texture Click the tool/menu indicated. Texture Generator Opens. Click Open at the left bottom of Texture Generator to open the texture image. The size and resolution of the textures loaded are displayed at the top. For XTEX files, other maps (Normal map, Opacity map etc.) in the folder are automatically loaded. Select Area of Texture Find and click on the minimum area where the fabric pattern repeats. Drag to select. The optimized result analyzed within the selected area will show up. The analyzed result is repeated in the preview window at the bottom. To adjust the area, move the point of the selected area. It is analyzed automatically again within the selected area. To maintain the selected area, click Manual at the right bottom of the selected area. The selected area is maintained and repeated. Set Options The options below can be set only in Auto mode since they work based on the analyzed results. Fabric Type Select fabric type for more accurate analysis. The analysis is based on Normal Map, thus it is only vaild with the existence of Normal Map. - Plain: Solid fabric without repeated patterns. - Repeat Pattern: Fabric pattern is regular. - Random Color Pattern: Fabric pattern is irregular. Equalize Adjust the value to equalize the difference in brightness caused by crease in the fabric. Note: Depending on the fabric, some colors or patterns may be distorted. Refer to the attached image. below. Smooth When the connected part of the fabrics are not smooth by crease in the fabric, align weave areas equally. Show/Hide Grid Click Show/Hide icon in Preview window at the bottom to check the grid of the repeated texture. Save Texture Image Click Save at the bottom to save the generated texture as Image file. Save Textures window appears. Select the textures and map type to save and click OK button. Each map name is automatically applied after the set name and saved as PNG files. Apply Texture When the texture generating is complete, click the Apply &amp Close button at the bottom right of Texture Generator. The texture is applied to the fabric simultaneously and the Texture generator is closed.

Title: Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials
Content: Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials Express Silk Express Velvet Express Glass Express Silk, Velvet and Glass Materials - Express fabric or other objects as silk, velvet, and glass. - Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Type. Express Silk - Select the object to be edited in the Object Browser. - In the Property Editor Material Type, select Fabric_Silk/Satin. - The selected object is expressed in silk material in the 3D window. Express Velvet - Select the object to be edited in the Object Browser. - In the Property Editor Material Type, select Fabric_Velvet. - The selected object is expressed in velvet material in the 3D window. Express Glass - Select the object to be edited in the Object Browser. - In the Property Editor Material Type, select Glass. - The selected object is expressed in glass material in the 3D window.

Title: glTF a Standard Fabric File Compatibility (ver 6.1)
Content: List of Contents Export Import Objective Import or export PBR material and the CLO's physical property as a glTF file. Operation Export Main Menu File Export Click Fabric (GLTF/GLB) menu. Save File window appears. Set the file saving path and name then click OK. Export gLTF window appears. Set the fabric you want to export and format then click OK. The selected fabric is exported as a glTF or GLB file. Note: Object Browser Fabric Tab You can also right-click on fabric items and Export (GLTF/GLB) menu. It's not possible to export the fabric with Substance (SBSAR) material due to the license issue. Import Main Menu File Import Click GLTF / GLB menu. or drag and drop the file in the 3D / 2D window. Import window appears. Change the type of object to Fabric and click OK. Import Fabric window appears. Select the desired fabric and click OK. The fabric is added to the Fabric Tab in the Object Browser. Note: You can also drag and drop a GLTF/GLB file in the fabric item or the fabric tab in the Object Browser.

Title: Assign to New Fabric
Content: Assign to New Fabric Assign to New Fabric - Add a new fabric item and apply it to the selected Patterns simultaneously. - Select Patterns using the Transform Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the Patterns to access the pop-up menu. Select Assign to New Fabric. A new fabric item will be added and applied to the selected Patterns.

Title: Open/Save Fabric File
Content: Objective Save a frequently used Fabric as a .zfab file or open a saved Fabric file to reuse. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Open/Save Operation General Click the tool/menu indicated. Click the fabric item and the Open/Save button in the Property Editor. The Save Fabric window will appear when saving. 옵션 설명 Preview Image Texture Image is applied by default, It can be set to Custom Image. Texture Image (ver 2024.1) If the texture image has transparency, choose to include or remove the transparency. After setting the save options, click the OK button to save. The fabric will be saved as a ZFAB file with the selected options. The fabric with the sel properties will be saved as a ZFAB file. Select Material Click the tool/menu indicated. Right-click on the fabric item Click the Open (Select Material) menu. Load Fabric window appears. Select a Zfab file. Open Fabric window appears. Select the items desired and click the OK button. The selected items are reflected in the fabric properties. Note: Press Ctrl on the keyboard while dragging and dropping the fabric file to the fabric item to open the 'Select Material window'.

Title: Fabric List Window
Content: Default_Fabric is provided as default Fabric, and being displayed in the Fabric list. When editing Default_Fabric, the edited default Fabric maintains until reopen a garment or rerun a program. It is able to reset edited properties of Default_Fabric at right-click pop-up menu.

Title: Reset Fabric Property
Content: Objective Reset a Fabric in order to return to a default Fabric properties. Location 2D Pattern Window Edit Texture (2D) Right-click Pattern Pop-up Menu Reset to Basic Fabric Object Browser Right-click Fabric List Pop-up Menu Reset Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Pattern Window Edit Texture(2D) Right-click Pattern Pop-up Menu Reset to Basic Fabric Object Browser Right-click Fabric List Pop-up Menu Reset The selected Fabric's texture, color and physical properties are now being reset.

Title: Fabric Information
Content: Objective Enter information of fabric. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Operation Select the tool/menu indicated. Select a fabric item. The properties appear in the Property Editor. Refer to the table below and enter the information Information (ver 6.1) Click the button to the right of the information menu to check the revision history of the fabric file. Name Enter the name of the fabric. The name is also reflected to the Fabric List. Item No. Enter the Item No. of the fabric. Classification Type in the content and classification. Supplier/ Owner (ver 6.0) The supplier and owner entered during fabric creation in Emulator mode are displayed. Note: Such fabric information can be previewed in the Library.

Title: Add & Apply Fabric Style
Content: List of Contents Add &amp Apply Group Setting (ver 7.1) Objective Add fabric style and apply it to the garment. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Operation Add &amp Apply Select the tool/menu indicated. Click Add at the top right. Or add a Fabric file by dragging it to the Fabric tab. A Fabric style is added. Drag the style to the 3D/2D pattern and apply it. Or after selecting a pattern first, click the Assign button to the right of the Fabric tab or Fabric style. The Fabric is applied to the pattern. Group Setting (ver 7.1) To set Fabric Groups, Click the Create New Folder button at the top left of the Fabric tab. A new folder group is created. Click the Add Fabric or Open Fabric Files buttons on the right side of the group to load the Fabric file. A Fabric style is added or opened to the group. Click the Edit Folder Name button on the left of the group to edit the name. Or drag the Fabric style to another group to change the group.

Title: Edit Texture
Content: List of Contents Move Zoom In/Out and Rotate Rotate Grainline Setting options Objective Modify the Fabric's grainline and location for individual Patterns, and texture image's rotation and size for individual Fabric. Location Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Texture Operation Move Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click Drag texture image applied to Pattern with the left mouse button. The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being moved. Zoom In/Out and Rotate Select the tool/menu indicated. Select a pattern with fabric applied. A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. Click on the diagonal, vertical, horizontal lines of the gizmo drag, or drag along the gizmo circle. Diagonal line : The size of the texture image is adjusted while the aspect ratio is maintained. Horizontal/ Vertical: Texture images are scaled only in the vertical and horizontal directions. Circle : The texture image is rotated. Or select a Fabric and enter the image's Width and Height value in Property Editor Material Texture Transformation. Note: Right-click to input the exact values while rotating textures and grainlines. Edit back of texture when you change Garment Rendering Style as Back Texture Surface. Rotate Grainline Select the tool/menu indicated. Select a Pattern to rotate the Fabric. A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. A circle appears when mouse-over the curve. Drag the grainline in the direction you want to rotate it. Simulate once it is adjusted. The draping is now being adjusted according to the change in grainline. Note: You can directly enter the angle in the Pattern Properties Fabric Grain Direction menu, and if you turn off the Link All Colorways menu, you can apply the different grain direction for each colorway. Setting options Select the tool/menu indicated. Right-click on the pattern and set options as needed. Menu Description Assign to New Fabric Apply new fabric to selected pattern. Reset to Basic Fabric Reset the fabric of the selected pattern to the properties of the basic fabric. Reset Fabric Angle Resets the texture angle to the original angle. Align Grain Aligns the grainline at an angle parallel to the X, Y, or custom axis. Match up Grain (ver 7.3) Align the grainline so that the texture between the selected segment and the baseline continues smoothly. For symmetrical patterns, the selected segment and symmetric line are matched. Delete Texture Delete the texture. Flip Texture Horizontally/ Vertically Flip the texture horizontally or vertically.

Title: Fabric
Content: List of Contents Fabric Add Fabric Item Copy Fabric Item Assign Fabric Item Reset Fabric Item Delete Fabric Item Fabric - In CLO, Fabric can be created just like how it is created in real life, applying texture to material properties. Add Fabric Item The Add Button - Click the Add button on the Object Browsers Fabric Tab. - A new Fabric Item will be added to the Object Browser. Drag &amp Drop - Drag and Drop the Fabric file from the Desktop to the Object Browser. - The selected file will be added to the Fabric list as a Fabric Item. Add From the Library Window - When there is a Fabric file in the Library Window, double-click the Fabric file to open. - The dialogue will appear to inform the user that the file has been added to the Object Browser. The selected file will be added to the Object Browser as a Fabric Item. Copy Fabric Item - Select the Fabric Item to be duplicated from the Object Browser. - Click the Copy button on the right side of the Fabric Item. - A new Fabric Item will be added having the same material properties with the selected Fabric Item. Assign Fabric Item - Select the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window and select the Pattern that a new Fabric Item will be applied to. - Locate and click the Assign button on the right top of the Object Browser. - A new Fabric Item will be added to the Object Browser and it will be automatically applied to the selected Pattern. Reset Fabric Item - Right-click on a Fabric Item which its settings will be reset and select Reset. - All settings such as texture, color, and material properties will be changed to default values. Delete Fabric Item - A Fabric Item can be deleted and the Delete icon will appear only when it is not applied to any Pattern. If the fabric Item is applied to any Pattern, it cannot be deleted and the Delete icon will disappear. - When the Delete icon does not appear next to the Fabric Item to be deleted, resolve the issue by following the steps below: - Select the Fabric Item to be deleted from the Object Browser. The Patterns applied with the selected Fabric Item will be highlighted in pink. - Navigate to the 2D window and right click on any Pattern highlighted in pink. Then, click Select All with Same Property Fabric - Apply other Fabric Items to the selected Patterns. Delete Icon - Select the Delete icon next to the Fabric Item. - The selected Fabric Item will be deleted from the Object Browser. Delete Option from the Right Click Pop-up Menu - Right-click on the Fabric Item to be deleted and select Delete from the pop-up window. - The selected Fabric Item will be deleted from the Object Browser. Delete key on Keyboard - Click the Fabric Item to be deleted and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. - The selected Fabric Item will be deleted from the Object Browser.

Title: Internal Rectangle
Content: List of Contents Internal Rectangle Create Internal Rectangle - Create a rectangle within a Pattern. - Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Rectangle - 2D Toolbar Internal Rectangle Create Create - Click and drag within a Pattern to create a rectangle in the 2D window. - To create a square, hold down the Shift key from the keyboard while click and drag. Create with Specific Values - Click within a Pattern to create an Internal Rectangle with specific values. - The Create Rectangle window appears. Size Set width and height of the Internal Rectangle. Replicate Interval : Set the distance between each replicated rectangles. Angle : Set the angle between each replicated rectangles. Number of Shapes : Set the number of rectangles to be replicated. Position Outline : Configure the rectangles location by setting the its outlines offset from the Pattern outlines left, right, top, and bottom. Center : Configure the rectangles location by setting the its centers offset from the Pattern outlines left, right, top, and bottom.

Title: Auto Fitting
Content: Objective Automatically fit patterns to an avatar's size. Note: Auto Fitting is supported with CLO avatars and any custom avatars that have a Fitting Suit applied. Note: This feature was previously called Auto Grading (v 7.2 and below). Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Auto Fitting 2D Toolbar Auto Fitting Operation Adjust the avatar size and drape 3D garments on the avatar. Note: Please set Particle Distance as 20mm for the most optimized result. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Auto Fitting 2D Toolbar Auto Fitting The Auto Fitting window appears. Adjust the below options as needed and click OK. Maintain Pattern Curvature(%) Configure the extent of modification of pattern curvature. Higher the value is, less affected curvature while resizing the patterns. On the other hand, lower the value is, both curvature and size of the patterns are modified. Maintain Graphic Size ON Graphics maintain their size. OFF The size of graphics are adjusted based on the size changes of the patterns. The 3D garment is auto-fitted and draped on the avatar.

Title: Creator's Field Guide
Content: Download our Creator's Field Guide that highlights main features and functions of the program.

Title: How long will it take me to learn CLO?
Content: The learning pace for CLO software differs for each individual and depends on the hours of practice and the complexity of your project. Therefore, it is hard to estimate the learning period, but everyone can reach a professional level after a certain practice. Some CLO users get it quickly through online tutorials on various channels and communicating with other CLO users via CLO community forum. If you could build your network, you may be able to acquire more extensive knowledge than others. For more information, please refer to the article about the Available Training Resources.

Title: Delete Graphics
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary graphic images. Operation Select a graphic image with Edit Texture 2D tool, Transform Graphic tool in the 2D window. Right-click on the graphic: Graphics pop-up menu Delete The selected graphic is deleted.

Title: Buttons: Change Thread Type and Material
Content: List of Contents Change Thread Type and Material Change Thread Type for Buttons Change Material for Buttons Change Thread Type and Material - Change thread type, material and color for the button thread. - Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Change Thread Type for Buttons - Select the desired thread type. Change Material for Buttons - Choose the desired material for the button thread by navigating to Property Editor Material Thread tab. - Turn off Use Same Material as Button option to apply different material to the button thread.

Title: Create Binding
Content: Objective Easily create Binding along Pattern Outlines. Location Main Menu Materials Binding Binding 3D Toolbar Binding Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Binding can be created appear in dashed lines. On a 3D Garment or 2D Pattern, click the start point and double click where you want to finish the Binding. Binding is created on the selected segment. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. The pattern of the Binding is displayed in the Print Layout Mode. (ver 7.1)

Title: Create POM
Content: List of Contents Single Group Objective Create rulers to check measurements of particular parts of 2D Patterns/Internal Shapes/Graphics. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Pattern Measure Point of Measure 2D Toolbar Point of Measure Operation Select the tool/menu indicated above. Left-click on a pattern or internal line to start creating a ruler. Single 3. Double click the endpoint or hit Enter to complete creating the ruler. A single POM is created and added to Object Browser POM Tab. Group 3. Double click the endpoint or hit Enter to complete creating the ruler. A group POM is created and added to Object Browser POM Tab as a single measurement. The length of the line linking two Patterns (one that is not placed within Patterns) is not included in the measurement. Note: Hold down the Shift key to display vertical, horizontal, and 45º guidelines based on the clicked point. To cancel while creating POM, press down the backspace key, ESC or Ctrl+Z (Windows)/Cmd+Z (Mac) keys on the keyboard. While creating POM, right-click to enter Distance Moved. Check 3D Length in the Property Editor after creating POM. Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines can be traced as POM. If there is grading information in the pattern that created the tape measure, the length is displayed by grading size in the POM tab. When creating a POM, press the P key on the keyboard to switch between the mode for generating it along a segment line and the mode for generating it as a polygon.(ver 2024.1)

Title: [Mac] Open an App from Unidentified Developer
Content: Objective Resolve issue when Open an App from Unidentified Developer message appears while installing or updating CLO in Mac. Operation When installing or updating CLO in Mac, Open an App from Unidentified Developer message may appear as below. Open Security &amp Privacy window. Choose Anywhere under Allow apps downloaded from. Note: If Anywhere option does not exist, select Mac App Store and identified developers. Save the changes. CLO will install or update properly. Reference: Apple Manual if needed.

Title: Scene and Render Properties File (ZSE)
Content: List of Contents Save Open Objective OBJ files imported as scene and props can be saved as a single file with render properties to be used for various garments. Location Main Menu Save as / Open Scene and Props Operation Save as Import OBJ files as scene and props. Set the render properties. Select the tool indicated in Location. Save Scene and Props window appears. Click the OK button after setting the thumbnail option. Auto The front view is applied as the thumbnail and preview image. Custom (ver 7.3) Apply desired images as the thumbnail and preview image. Click the Save button after setting the file namd and path. The OBJ file imported as scene and props along with the render properties are saved as a ZSE file Open Select the tool indicated in Location. Select the ZSE file to import and click the Open button. Add Scene and Props window appears. After setting the options, Click the OK button. Load Type Open or add the ZSE file. Object Select and import only among the scene and props and render properties saved in the ZSE file. The ZSE file is imported based on the setting. Note: By clicking on the objects imported as the Scene and Props and enabling the Collision option in the Property Editor, they will collide with the garment in simulation for a variety of looks. (ver 2024.0)

Location Main Menu Render Render via CLOSET Main Menu Display Window Render via CLOSET Main Menu Share Render via CLOSET Main Menu File Share Render via CLOSET Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu Render Render via CLOSET Main Menu Display Window Render via CLOSET Main Menu Share Render via CLOSET Main Menu File Share Render via CLOSET You are navigated to CLOSET.

Title: Camera Motion
Content: List of Contents Add KeyFrame Move/Delete KeyFrame Show/Hide Camera Path Save/Open Camera Motion File Objective Create more dynamic animations with various camera positions and angles. Location Animation Mode Operation Add KeyFrame Click where you want to add a keyframe on the timeline, or move the playhead to the desired position. Control the 3D Window view and click the Add/Replace Camera Keyframe button. Keyframes are added based on the state of the controlled view. If you want to move and rotate the camera yourself, click Camera ViewFinder button. The camera object is displayed in the 3D window, and the Camera Preview window (ViewFinder) appears. Note: The screen size of the camera preview window is applied according to the size set in the render image properties. The window screen size can be adjusted by clicking and dragging the bottom right corner. Click the camera or the point displayed on the target of the camera in the 3D window. Gizmo appears. Click and drag each axis of the gizmo to move it directly, or enter each value directly in the property editor. A keyframe for that camera is added to the timeline at the position of the playhead. Note: Click the group button at the top right of the gizmo to simultaneously move and rotate the camera and its position relative to its target. After selecting the added keyframe, then adjust the view. The camera view of the keyframe is changed. Move/Delete KeyFrame Click and drag the added keyframe to the desired position. The keyframe is moved to that position. Or right-click on the keyframe you want to delete. The keyframe is deleted. Show/Hide Camera Path Click the Show Camera Path button. Shows or hides paths between camera positions for each keyframe. Save/Open Camera Motion File Click Main Menu Save As/Open Camera Motion. A camera motion file (CAK) is saved or opened.

Title: Create/Edit V-Ray Lights (ver 5.2)
Content: List of Contents Create Light Select/ Move/ Rotate Light Right-click Pop-up Menu Objective Create and edit various lights. Location Create Light Render Toolbar Rectangle/Sphere/Spot/Directional/IES/ Dome Light Select Light Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Create Light Select the tool indicated in Location. Content: List of Contents Copy Save Objective Easily use the preview image in the Render window by copying and saving the preview. Note: The image appears in the Render window is a preview image, whereas the final render image is a high quality image which all render, light, and image/video properties are fully applied. Location Copy Render Toolbar Copy Current Image Save Render Toolbar Save Current Image Operation Copy Follow the indicated guideline below: Render Toolbar Copy Current Image The preview image in the Render window is copied to the clipboard and can be pasted to other programs as needed. Save Follow the indicated guideline below: Render Toolbar Save Current Image The Save Image File window appears. Name the image and designate the saving path. Then, select Save. The image is saved.

Title: 3D File (OBJ) Import/Export
Content: List of Contents Import/ Import (Add) OBJ Export OBJ Import OBJs as avatars, trims, and garments. Note: 3D garments created in CLO can be exported as OBJ and compatible with other 3D software. An MTL file which saves material properties of the exported 3D garment is created at the time of OBJ export. Import/ Import (Add) OBJ Click the Main Menu File Import/Import (Add) OBJ Select ta desired file and click Open. Click OK after configuring options. Object Type Load as Avatar Load an OBJ as an avatar to drape garments. Automatically Add Arrangement Points - Arrangement Points are automatically created based on the OBJ. Note: Arrangement Points are properly created only when avatars are in either A or T-pose. Load as Trim Load an OBJ as a trim. OBJs imported as trims do not calculate collision. Load as Garment Import and simulate an OBJ created in other 3D software such as Maya, 3ds Max, etc.). Toggle on Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map to automatically generate patterns based on the UV information. Load as Morph Target Load an OBJ to morph already imported OBJ. Configure Morphing Frame Count to control morphing speed. Higher the value is, slower the morphing is. Note: Morphing refers to a method to transform appearance of an OBJ according to another OBJ. For CLO avatars, users can modify the shape or pose by using Avatar Size Editor or Show X-Ray Joints features, but users cannot easily change imported OBJs created in other 3D software due to un-rigged joints or loss of joint information. Thus, users can utilize Load as Morph Target feature to change body shape or pose of the imported OBJ. However, to do so, users need two or more OBJ files with the identical mesh structure. Scale Type in the Scale or select the desired unit. Axis Conversion Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. Translation Locate the import position of the OBJ. Toggle on Align Bottom to Ground to surface the OBJ when it is located below the ground. Export OBJ Click the Main Menu File Export OBJ/OBJ(Selected) menu. Locate the saving path and click Save. Configure the options and click OK. Object Select All Patterns Select or deselect all Patterns. Select All Avatars Select or deselect all avatars/ objects. Select All Graphics/ Top-stitches Select or deselect all graphics or top-stitches. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Single Object/Multiple Objects Choose to export as a single object or multiple objects. Unweld/ Weld Choose to export vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects or a single point. Thin/ Thick Choose to export the object with thickness or not. Combined UV Coordinates A combined UV coordinates is also exported. Include Internal Shape Export with internal line and/or shape information . Scale Scale the exported object's size. Axis Conversion Change directions of object's each axis. File Save Colorway Export colorway along with the *.obj file. Maintain Individual Texture Image Coordinates Each colorway is exported individually as *.obj and *.mtl files. Share Texture Image Coordinates All colorways are exported as a single *.obj and as many *.mtl files as colorways. Save with Absolute Texture Image File Path Export OBJ to the original file's saving path. Note: When there is not image file at the original path, it may get lost as this option only saves the path. Save with Texture Files (ZIP) Export OBJs along with textures. Diffuse Color Combined on Texture When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting. Exclude Ambient Map &amp Color (Modo) Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting. Save with Transparency Map Extracted from Diffuse Map Alpha Map is included when exporting. Save with Meta Data(XML) Exports garment's patter(Mesh), physical property and sewing information as Meta Data. Combine and save garment's texture image and color as a single image.

Title: "MSVCP100.dll was not found" error - troubleshooting
Content: When running the CLO software, it may not run with the following error. This is caused by missing or outdated Visual C++ Redistributable which essential Windows components to running CLO software. How to solve Visit Microsoft website, then download and install the latest Visual C++ Redistributable. The X64 architecture recommended. Note In some cases, you may need to remove older versions of the Visual C++ Redistributable installed on your computer. The Visual C++ Redistributable is backwards compatible with older versions, so we recommend installing only the most recent version.

Title: When macOS displays a warning on first launch
Content: Problem Situations When launch CLO, macOS shows that it is an unverified developer's app. When launch CLO, macOS shows that it is a malicious software. macOS shows that CLO is an app downloaded from the Internet. How to solve First, please make sure that you must download the CLO app from CLO official website. CLO software is distributed after being signed by a verified developer and notarized by Apple. 1 Simply click the Show in Finder then RIGHT CLICK and select Open. 2 It will give you a similar Error, but OPEN will be an option. Just Click Open and you should be fine. References Since the release of macOS Catalina, Apple has changed the macOS policy to: About the security content of macOS Catalina 10.15 Change Security &amp Privacy General preferences on Mac Open a Mac app from an unidentified developer Find out which macOS your Mac is using

Title: CLO Silent Install (No GUI Install)
Content: You can install CLO software without a GUI using the commands described below. This is convenient when installing CLO software in an environment with multiple PCs, such as a school and company. Windows 1 Search for Command Prompt (CMD) in Windows Search and run it as administrator. 2 Enter the following into the Command Prompt: CLO_Network_OnlineAuth_7_2_116_Installer_x64.exe /S /USERNAME=&ltWindows Login ID&gt /D=&ltCLO install path&gt eg) CLO_Network_OnlineAuth_7_2_116_Installer_x64.exe /S /USERNAME=johndoe /D=C:Program FilesCLO Network OnlineAuth_7.2.116 Enter the above command in the path where the CLO installer is saved. USERNAME is the user name you see when you log in to Windows. Depending on your Windows login permissions, a User Account Control warning window may appear. If you see a UAC warning, click Yes to continue the installation. macOS 1 Download the attached script file. 2 Run Terminal.app on your Mac. 3 Enter the following into the Terminal: sh install_clo_dmg.sh /Users/&ltusername&gt/downloads/CLO_Network_OnlineAuth_7_2_116_Installer.dmg CLO_Standalone_OnlineAuth.app eg) sh install_clo_dmg.sh /Users/johndoe/downloads/CLO_Network_OnlineAuth_7_2_116_Installer.dmg CLO_Network_OnlineAuth.app USERNAME is the user name you see when you log in to Mac. For macOS, the App name you must enter varies depending on the type of CLO product you want to install. Please check the product name carefully before entering it. CLO_Network_OnlineAuth CLO_Network CLO_Standalone_OnlineAuth CLO_Standalone
